steps: Take an initial quantity of 100 units.
It first becomes 120 and then 120×0.8=96.
The final value is 4 units below 100, a 4% decrease.

question: A and B finish a job alone in 6 and 3 hours respectively. At constant independent work rates, find their completion time together in hours.

steps: Add the independent rates: 1/6+1/3=1/2 job/hour.
The whole job therefore takes 1/(1/2) hours.
Combined completion time is 2 hours.
commonMistakes: Add work rates, not completion times.

hints: Identify the conditions under which work rates applies.
Start from $ 1/T=1/T_A+1/T_B $.

verification.method: Add conserved work rates before taking reciprocal. Arithmetic checked by executable calculation/property fixtures; same-system solution review only.

question: How many distinct arrangements of the letters in LEVEL are possible?

steps: If the five positions were all distinct there would be 5!=120 permutations.
Exchanging the identical L letters or identical E letters does not create a new arrangement.
Divide by 2!×2!=4 to get 30.
commonMistakes: Do not divide by an additional 2 for V, which occurs only once.

hints: Identify the conditions under which permutations with repetitions applies.
Start from $ N=\frac{5!}{2!2!} $.

verification.method: Enumerate all positional permutations and deduplicate actual strings. Arithmetic checked by executable calculation/property fixtures; same-system solution review only.

question: All members of set A belong to set B. No member of B belongs to C. Which conclusion necessarily follows?

options.text: Some B must belong to A

solution.formula: A\subseteq B,\ B\cap C=\varnothing\Rightarrow A\cap C=\varnothing
steps: Any hypothetical member of A is also a member of B.
Since no B member can be in C, that same member cannot be in C.
Thus A and C are disjoint. The premises do not assert that A is nonempty, so an existential conclusion is not forced.
solution.explanation: Thus A and C are disjoint. The premises do not assert that A is nonempty, so an existential conclusion is not forced.
commonMistakes: Universal statements do not necessarily assert existence.

hints: Identify the conditions under which set-based deduction applies.
Start from $ A\subseteq B,\ B\cap C=\varnothing\Rightarrow A\cap C=\varnothing $.

verification.method: Set-subset/disjoint deduction; check empty-set and nonempty counterexamples to existential alternatives. Arithmetic checked by executable calculation/property fixtures; same-system solution review only.

question: A right circular cylinder has radius 2 cm and height 3 cm. Find its volume divided by π, in cm³.

steps: The base area is π×2²=4π cm².
Multiply by height 3 cm to get 12π cm³.
The requested value V/π is 12 cm³.
solution.explanation: The requested value V/π is 12 cm³.
commonMistakes: The prompt asks for volume divided by π, not the full decimal volume.

hints: Identify the conditions under which cylinder volume applies.
Start from $ V=\pi r^2h $.

verification.method: Integrate constant cross-sectional area divided by π along cylinder height. Arithmetic checked by executable calculation/property fixtures; same-system solution review only.

question: In a class of 40 students, 25 study subject A, 20 study B and 10 study both. How many study neither?

steps: Adding 25+20 counts the 10 students in both subjects twice.
Subtract their overlap once: union size 35.
The number studying neither is 40−35=5.
commonMistakes: Do not subtract the overlap twice when forming the union.

hints: Identify the conditions under which inclusion–exclusion applies.
Start from $ |A\cup B|=|A|+|B|-|A\cap B| $.

verification.method: Inclusion–exclusion accounting of membership counts. Arithmetic checked by executable calculation/property fixtures; same-system solution review only.

question: Two fair six-sided dice are rolled independently. Find the probability that their sum equals 7.

given: 36 equally likely ordered pairs of die outcomes
steps: There are 6 favorable ordered pairs out of 36.
Probability is 6/36=1/6.
commonMistakes: The two dice form ordered outcomes, even when the sum ignores order.

hints: Identify the conditions under which counting ordered outcomes applies.
Start from $ P(E)=N_E/N_S $.

question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence for the stated singular subject “Each of the instruments”.

options.text: Each of the instruments are calibrated.
Each of the instruments is calibrated.
Each of the instruments were calibrated tomorrow.
Each of the instruments have calibrated.

given: Subject headed by singular distributive pronoun Each
steps: The grammatical head of the subject is Each, not instruments inside the of-phrase.
A singular present-tense subject takes is in this passive construction.
Therefore “Each of the instruments is calibrated” is correct. The other options have agreement or tense/structure errors.
solution.explanation: Therefore “Each of the instruments is calibrated” is correct. The other options have agreement or tense/structure errors.
commonMistakes: Do not make the verb agree with a nearby plural noun inside a prepositional phrase.

hints: Identify the conditions under which subject–verb agreement applies.
Start from $ \text{Each}\ \longrightarrow\ \text{singular finite verb} $.

verification.method: Singular distributive subject head “Each” controls finite-verb agreement; language-rule review, not a numeric check. Arithmetic checked by executable calculation/property fixtures; same-system solution review only.

question: Point P=(2,1) is rotated by 90° counterclockwise about the origin, then translated by (3,−1). Find the final x-coordinate.

solution.asked: Find the x-coordinate after both transformations.
steps: Rotating (2,1) gives (−1,2).
Add the translation vector (3,−1) to obtain (2,1).
The final x-coordinate is 2. Rotation and translation generally do not commute.
solution.explanation: The final x-coordinate is 2. Rotation and translation generally do not commute.
commonMistakes: Apply transformations in the specified order.

hints: Identify the conditions under which planar rotation and translation applies.
Start from $ (x,y)\xrightarrow{90^\circ\ CCW}(-y,x) $.

verification.method: Matrix rotation followed by explicit translation. Arithmetic checked by executable calculation/property fixtures; same-system solution review only.

question: Three jobs A,B,C must be ordered. A must precede B, and C must not be first. Which complete orders satisfy both constraints?

steps: A B C places A before B and C third, so it is valid.
C A B violates the first-position rule, whereas A C B satisfies both rules.
B A C violates A-before-B. Select A and C.

hints: Identify the conditions under which constraint-based ordering applies.
Start from $ \operatorname{pos}(A)<\operatorname{pos}(B),\quad\operatorname{pos}(C)\ne1 $.
